From ea104a9e4d3e9ebc26fb78dac35585b142ee288b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Michael Walle <michael@walle.cc>
Date: Fri, 27 Mar 2020 17:24:50 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] watchdog: sp805: fix restart handler

The restart handler is missing two things, first, the registers
has to be unlocked and second there is no synchronization for the
write_relaxed() calls.

This was tested on a custom board with the NXP LS1028A SoC.

Fixes: 6c5c0d48b686c ("watchdog: sp805: add restart handler")
Signed-off-by: Michael Walle <michael@walle.cc>
Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200327162450.28506-1-michael@walle.cc
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Signed-off-by: Wim Van Sebroeck <wim@linux-watchdog.org>

diff --git a/drivers/watchdog/sp805_wdt.c b/drivers/watchdog/sp805_wdt.c
index 53e04926a7b2..190d26e2e75f 100644
--- a/drivers/watchdog/sp805_wdt.c
+++ b/drivers/watchdog/sp805_wdt.c
@@ -137,10 +137,14 @@ wdt_restart(struct watchdog_device *wdd, unsigned long mode, void *cmd)
 {
 	struct sp805_wdt *wdt = watchdog_get_drvdata(wdd);
 
+	writel_relaxed(UNLOCK, wdt->base + WDTLOCK);
 	writel_relaxed(0, wdt->base + WDTCONTROL);
 	writel_relaxed(0, wdt->base + WDTLOAD);
 	writel_relaxed(INT_ENABLE | RESET_ENABLE, wdt->base + WDTCONTROL);
 
+	/* Flush posted writes. */
+	readl_relaxed(wdt->base + WDTLOCK);
+
 	return 0;
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/watchdog/sp805_wdt.c`**
1. Added a line to unlock the registers by writing `UNLOCK` to `wdt->base + WDTLOCK`.
2. Added a line to ensure synchronization for the `write_relaxed()` calls by reading from `wdt->base + WDTLOCK` to flush posted writes.

### Relationships
The modifications in the `sp805_wdt.c` file address two critical issues in the `wdt_restart` function: 
- The first change ensures that the watchdog registers are unlocked before any control operations are performed, which is necessary for the proper functioning of the restart handler.
- The second change introduces a mechanism to synchronize the write operations, ensuring that all previous writes are completed before proceeding, which helps prevent potential race conditions or inconsistent states. 

Together, these changes enhance the reliability and correctness of the watchdog restart functionality.

watchdog: sp805: fix restart handler

The restart handler is missing two things, first, the registers
has to be unlocked and second there is no synchronization for the

This was tested on a custom board with the NXP LS1028A SoC.

Fixes: 6c5c0d48b686c ("watchdog: sp805: add restart handler")
Signed-off-by: Michael Walle <michael@walle.cc>
Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200327162450.28506-1-michael@walle.cc
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Signed-off-by: Wim Van Sebroeck <wim@linux-watchdog.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of register unlocking and lack of synchronization for the `write_relaxed()` calls in the `wdt_restart` function, which could lead to improper handling of the watchdog restart process and potential race conditions.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int
 wdt_restart(struct watchdog_device *wdd, unsigned long mode, void *cmd)
 {
 	struct sp805_wdt *wdt = watchdog_get_drvdata(wdd);
 
+	writel_relaxed(UNLOCK, wdt->base + WDTLOCK);
 	writel_relaxed(0, wdt->base + WDTCONTROL);
 	writel_relaxed(0, wdt->base + WDTLOAD);
 	writel_relaxed(INT_ENABLE | RESET_ENABLE, wdt->base + WDTCONTROL);
 
+	/* Flush posted writes. */
+	readl_relaxed(wdt->base + WDTLOCK);
+
 	return 0;
 }

The absence of register unlocking and lack of synchronization for the `write_relaxed()` calls can lead to improper handling of the watchdog restart process, as these writes may not be executed in the intended order or may be interrupted, resulting in race conditions.
